PB times per Long Rest, when you fail a D20 Test spend and roll a Hit Die and add it (once per test). If the die shows its highest or lowest number, you regain that Hit Die.
When a creature moves you without using your movement, take a Reaction to reduce the distance by up to your Speed. Advantage on saves that would apply a condition.

A Study action identifies a magic item's properties and use without attuning (not curses), with a cumulative 5% chance per rarity step above Common of getting it wrong. You start with a Common magic item chosen with your GM.
On your first turn after rolling Initiative, add 1d4 to your first damage roll (2d4 at level 9, 4d4 at level 16). HP maximum increases by your character level, and by 1 per level after.

Blood and Bone: Utilize action and a Healer's Kit use lets a creature within 5 feet spend and roll a Hit Die to heal. Bedside Manner: whenever you restore HP or use Blood and Bone, roll one extra die and drop the lowest.

+1 Dexterity, Constitution, or Intelligence (max 20). No Disadvantage at long range with Blackpowder Pistols, ignore their Loading property, and when a creature within 5 feet of you moves, take a Reaction to shoot it with one.

+1 Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution (max 20). A Versatile weapon used in one hand deals its two-handed damage in melee. When an effect would make you drop what you hold, make a DC 15 Strength save to keep it, and you have Advantage on saves to keep your grip.

+1 Strength or Constitution (max 20). Once per turn an Unarmed Strike hit deals +1d4 Bludgeoning. Add Str mod to Intimidation, Performance, and Persuasion checks. Count one size larger (max Large) for carrying.

+1 Strength, Constitution, or Charisma (max 20). Advantage on saves against Poisoned and on Survival checks to forage. Once per Short or Long Rest, as a Bonus Action spend a Hit Die and heal its roll + Con mod.

display.prerequisite: Level 4+, Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature
display.description: +1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (max 20). When you cast a single-target action cantrip, a Bonus Action lets it target a second creature in range. Once per Long Rest, a spell you cast as a Reaction uses no slot.
Blood and Bone lets the creature spend up to three Hit Dice, or spend three to end Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or Stunned instead of healing (or cure one Grievous Wound).

+1 Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution (max 20). Without armor or a Shield, Dodge as a Bonus Action. While Grappled or Restrained your attacks don't have Disadvantage and attacks against you don't have Advantage.

display.prerequisite: Level 4+, Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature
display.description: Pick a Sangromancy spell of a level you have slots for: always prepared, once per Long Rest without a slot, or with slots. You also have two d12 Sangromancy Dice to spend instead of Hit Dice on Sangromancy spells, refilled on a Long Rest.

display.prerequisite: Level 4+, Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature
display.description: +1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (max 20). Shadowsteel curses are always prepared and castable with any slots. While holding your Shadowsteel Focus, +1 to spell attacks and spell save DCs, and if it is a weapon it is +1.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (max 20). With your Shadowsteel Focus, one creature you hit or that fails a save against your slot spell takes 1d4 Necrotic per slot level. A weapon Focus becomes +2 and once per turn adds 2d8 Necrotic on a hit.

Proficiency with Thieves' Tools (craft a key in 10 minutes with the lock), Disguise Kit (10-minute costume changes your apparent features and even species, not size or shape), and Forgery Kit (no word limit mimicking handwriting). Hide from non-Hostile creatures while only Lightly Obscured, using Charisma if you like.

+1 Strength or Dexterity (max 20). After an Attack action with a Simple Thrown weapon, make two more Simple Thrown attacks as a Bonus Action. As a Bonus Action, gather and stow or wield all Simple Thrown weapons within 5 feet (free hand needed). Your proficient Simple Thrown weapons gain the Returning property.

+1 Strength, Constitution, or Wisdom (max 20). When a spell targets only you with no area, take a Reaction for a Wisdom save against its DC; on a success the caster must pick a new target or the spell is wasted. Melee or Unarmed Strike hits on spellcasters cut their Speed by 15 feet until your next turn. Advantage on saves against Shadowsteel curses and spells lasting over 10 minutes.

display.prerequisite: Fighting Style feature (or level 8+ as a General feat)
display.description: Proficiency with Advanced weapons, including use of their mastery properties.
Being within 5 feet of an enemy doesn't give your Ranged weapon attacks Disadvantage, and your ranged hits on creatures within 5 feet deal +2 damage.
When you attack with a bow or crossbow as part of the Attack action, you can add one extra attack against a creature within 10 feet of the first target; both attacks have Disadvantage.
Once per turn, give up Advantage on a weapon or Unarmed Strike attack; afterward attack a different creature within 5 feet of the first target and in reach.
When you take the Attack action, your Speed increases by 10 feet and Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage until the end of your turn.
Attacks you make as part of a Reaction get +2 to attack and damage rolls.
Being Prone doesn't give your attacks Disadvantage or attacks against you Advantage, and standing up costs only 5 feet of movement.
+1 Intelligence or Wisdom (max 30). Once per Short or Long Rest, turn a failed saving throw into a success.
+1 Strength or Dexterity (max 30). Fly Speed 40 feet with hover, and falls slow to 60 feet per round.
+1 Strength (max 20). Wield a Two-Handed melee weapon in one hand, and a Versatile melee weapon held in one hand counts as Light.

+1 Charisma (max 20). As an action, an ally within 60 feet who hears you can immediately use its Reaction to Attack (one attack), Dash, Dodge, Hide, Influence, Search, Study, or Utilize. Enemies can't have Advantage on attacks against you while you're within 5 feet of two or more active allies.
+1 Strength or Dexterity (max 20). Your weapon and Unarmed Strike attacks crit on 19 or 20.

+1 Strength or Dexterity (max 20). +2 AC against attacks from creatures whose CR exceeds your level. Advantage on attacks against a creature that dropped an ally to 0 HP since your last turn. PB times per Long Rest, take a Reaction to stop a Legendary Action you can see.

+1 Int, Wis, or Cha (max 20). Find Familiar always prepared, once per Long Rest as a Magic action with no slot or components; your familiar can also be an Imp, Pseudodragon, Quasit, Sphinx of Wonder, or Sprite. PB times per Long Rest, take a Reaction to give Disadvantage to an attack made by a creature within 5 feet of your familiar.

+1 Int, Wis, or Cha (max 20). When casting a spell that scales, spend an extra slot to raise its effective level by 1 (max 9). Or cast a spell with a higher slot at its base level and regain a level 1 slot.
+1 Int, Wis, or Cha (max 20). Your magic items' save DCs can use 8 + that ability's modifier + PB if higher. Once per Long Rest, after a Short Rest, recharge one magic item as if it were dawn.

display.prerequisite: Level 4+, Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature
display.description: +1 Int, Wis, or Cha (max 20). When you fail a D20 Test, spend a spell slot to add 2 + its level. Once per Long Rest, after a Short Rest, spend up to PB Hit Dice to recover spell slots of that total level.

+1 Int, Wis, or Cha (max 20). Learn Fire Bolt and always have Burning Hands and Scorching Ray prepared, each once per Long Rest without a slot. When a Fire damage die rolls its maximum, roll it again and add it, repeating, up to PB extra dice.
+1 Str or Dex (max 20). When you roll Initiative without Disadvantage, draw a weapon and attack with it. Your Speed is doubled during the first round of combat.

+1 Cha (max 20). Performance proficiency, or Expertise if you have it. PB times per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action taunt a creature within 15 feet that can hear you: Disadvantage on its next attack against anyone else before the end of its next turn.

+1 Int, Wis, or Cha (max 20). Learn two of Arc Blade, Burning Blade, Frigid Blade, or True Strike (swappable each level), and replace one Attack action attack with casting one. PB times per Long Rest, add your Int, Wis, or Cha mod (min +1) to a proficient weapon attack roll.

An obvious augmentation of your choice. Aquatic Adaptation: breathe water and Swim Speed equal to your Speed. Natural Armor: AC 13 + Dex or Con mod. Natural Weapons: Unarmed Strikes deal 1d8 Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing. Night Vision: Darkvision 60 feet (or +30).

Old Blessing: once per Long Rest cast Bless only on creatures carrying your wicker charms (or with slots), using Int, Wis, or Cha. Twisted Hex: as a Magic action curse a charm with an ability; whoever carries it, or whose home holds it, has Disadvantage on checks and attacks with that ability, and on such a failure can make a Cha save (DC 8 + PB + that modifier) to destroy it. One hex charm at a time.

Learn the Blood Bolt cantrip (Int, Wis, or Cha). After a Long Rest, a 1-minute ritual bleeds up to PB Hit Dice into a vial; a creature drinking it as a Bonus Action rolls those dice and heals the total + its Con mod. It keeps until your next Long Rest.

Learn two Warlock cantrips and always have one level 1 Warlock spell prepared, castable once per Short or Long Rest without a slot or with slots (Int, Wis, or Cha). Swap one choice when you gain a level.

Eldritch Word: as a Bonus Action a creature within 60 feet makes a Wis save (DC 8 + PB + Int, Wis, or Cha mod) or is Frightened until your next turn; free once per Short or Long Rest, and extra uses cost you 1d6 Necrotic that can't be reduced. Shred Fate: Bane always prepared, once per Long Rest without a slot or Material components.

Gain Heroic Inspiration (if you lack it) when you win a contested check, drop a creature to 0 HP, or a creature fails a save you forced, unless it has no CR or CR 0. As a Bonus Action spend Heroic Inspiration for temp HP equal to your level.

Ignore the damage Resistances of creatures with Incorporeal Movement. Once per Short or Long Rest after a detection, as a Bonus Action sense the distance and direction of Undead and Ethereal creatures within 60 feet.

Gain one Channel Divinity use for Turn Undead (DC 8 + Wis mod + PB), or add a use to an existing Channel Divinity. A 10-minute rite with 10 GP of trappings keeps a Medium or smaller corpse from becoming Undead.
As a Bonus Action study a creature; your next damage to it before your next turn ignores its Resistances. Advantage on checks to recall lore about creatures.
Advantage on Investigation checks, and on saves against Charmed and against having your memories read or altered.

A fool's mask and costume give you a separate identity that can get away with small affronts to authority. Hideous Laughter always prepared, once per Long Rest without a slot or Material components (Int, Wis, or Cha).

You cast no reflection or shadow. Insight checks against you have Disadvantage. Among at least two creatures of your type within one size of you, you can Hide from those outside the group with Deception instead of Stealth, needing no cover; straying more than 5 feet from them reveals you.

+1 Constitution (max 20). Add Con mod (min 1) to Death Saving Throws. Once per Long Rest, an effect that would kill you outright or drop you to 0 HP without damage leaves you at HP equal to your level.

display.prerequisite: Level 4+, Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature
display.description: +1 Int, Wis, or Cha (max 20). Once per Long Rest, cast a 1-minute spell as an action.

Protective Aegis: once per Long Rest, when you or an ally within 10 feet takes damage, use your Reaction to reduce it by your Proficiency Bonus + Charisma modifier (minimum 1). Radiant Aura: as a Bonus Action, shed bright light 10 feet and dim light 10 more (Bonus Action to end). Sunlance: you know Sacred Flame (Charisma).

Cold Aegis: when you take Cold damage, use your Reaction to gain Resistance to Cold until the end of your next turn, Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest. Winter Magic: you know Ray of Frost and always have Armor of Agathys or Ice Knife prepared, castable once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots (Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma).

You have Vitality Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus per Long Rest. Vitality Surge: Bonus Action and 1 point to regain 1d4 Hit Points, or stabilize yourself while Dying (no action). Channel Vitality: Bonus Action and 1 point to heal a creature you touch 1d4.

Proficiency in Animal Handling or Nature. You learn Druidcraft and Thorn Whip and always have Entangle or Hail of Thorns prepared, castable once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots (Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma).

Poison Resilience: when you take Poison damage, use your Reaction to gain Resistance to Poison until the end of your next turn, Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest. Serpent Kinship: Animal Friendship and Speak with Animals always prepared, each once per Long Rest without a slot (snakes and serpents only) or with slots. You know Draconic.

Proficiency in Deception (Expertise if already proficient). You learn Minor Illusion and Vicious Mockery and always have Disguise Self or Charm Person prepared, castable once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots (Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma).

Gift of Dexterity: add your Proficiency Bonus to a Dexterity check (again if already added), Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest. You know True Strike and always have Hunter's Mark or Longstrider prepared, castable once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots.

Gift of Strength: add your Proficiency Bonus to a Strength check (again if already added), Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest. You know Shocking Grasp or Thunderclap and always have Thunderous Smite prepared, castable once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots.

Proficiency with one Artisan's Tool (Advantage with it if already proficient). You learn Elementalism and Mending and always have Burning Hands or Shield prepared, castable once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots.

Proficiency in Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion (Expertise if already proficient). You know Guidance and always have one level 1 spell of your choice prepared, castable once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots.

Proficiency with Brewer's Supplies and a 50% discount on food and drink. After a Long Rest with Brewer's Supplies you brew a mead; a creature that drinks it (Utilize action) gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. It keeps until your next Long Rest.
In water you have Advantage on saves against extreme cold and on Strength (Athletics) checks to swim. On a turn you dive from land into water, you swim at full Speed.
Proficiency in Survival. Advantage on d20 Tests to operate water vehicles. With access to water, 1 hour of fishing feeds up to 6 people for a day.

Fates' Favor: once per day, add your Proficiency Bonus to a d20 Test after seeing the roll. Fates' Scorn: once per day, subtract your Proficiency Bonus from another creature's attack roll or ability check after seeing the roll.
Proficiency with Navigator's Tools. Advantage on attack rolls and ability checks on a turn you exit the water or a ship.

Advantage on Strength (Athletics) and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks to board vehicles. When you score a melee Critical Hit, make another melee attack against that creature or an adjacent one as a Bonus Action.
Advantage on saves and checks to keep your balance on slippery surfaces and snow, and on Wisdom (Survival) checks in snowy or icy terrain.

Proficiency with one musical instrument and one of Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. Give yourself Advantage on an Intelligence (Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion) check Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest.

display.prerequisite: Level 4+, Strength 13+, Proficiency with Martial Weapons
display.description: +1 Strength. Once per turn when you hit with a Handaxe, attack with a Handaxe as a Bonus Action. Battleaxe Topple saves have Disadvantage. Greataxe Cleave reaches extra creatures equal to half your Proficiency Bonus.
+1 Strength. When you miss a ranged attack with a thrown Handaxe, use a Bonus Action that turn to catch it as it returns.

+1 Strength or Charisma. As a Bonus Action once per Short Rest, roll Charisma (Intimidation); a creature that can hear you within 30 feet makes a Wisdom save against the result or is Frightened for 1d4 rounds (save each turn). Two creatures at level 9; three and 60 feet at level 15.

display.prerequisite: Level 4+, Giantkin or Trollkin (or GM permission)
display.description: +1 Strength or Wisdom. Thunderous Strike: add 1d6 Thunder to a melee weapon hit, Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest. Prophetic Vision: once per Long Rest as a Magic action, cast a 1-action Divination spell of a level up to half your character level without a slot (Wisdom).
+1 Wisdom or Charisma. Proficiency in Persuasion and Advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks.

+1 Strength or Constitution. Proficiency in Perception (Expertise if already proficient), and give yourself Advantage on Perception checks Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest. Proficiency with the horn. Once per Long Rest, reroll Initiative and use the new result.

Advantage on Death Saving Throws. When you become Stable after a third success or are stabilized by another creature, regain 1d6 + Proficiency Bonus Hit Points. You know Spare the Dying and Toll the Dead (Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma).

+1 Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution. Cast Find Steed (a sea serpent) once per Long Rest without a slot, or with slots. You breathe water, automatically succeed on saves against extreme cold while submerged, and have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.
+1 Constitution. Once per Short or Long Rest, give yourself Advantage on a ranged weapon attack made with the Attack action. +10 feet Speed on ice or snow, which are never Difficult Terrain for you.

+1 Constitution. You know Ice Knife and can cast it without a slot Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest, or with slots. Once per Long Rest, turn a failed save against a Cold-damage spell or effect into a success.

+1 Strength or Charisma. Advantage on saves to avoid or end Frightened. Justicar: as a Magic action, touch a creature; on a failed Charisma save it can't deliberately lie for 1 minute (once per Long Rest per creature).

+1 Strength or Constitution. Once per Long Rest while Bloodied, enter a 1-minute fury as a Bonus Action: melee weapon attacks deal extra damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you don't fall Unconscious at 0 Hit Points (you still make Death Saves).
+1 Constitution. While Bloodied, when you take damage, spend a Hit Die as a Reaction to reduce it by the roll. A successful Strength or Constitution save against half-damage effects means no damage.
+1 Constitution. When you take damage, +1 to saves until the end of your next turn; while Bloodied, +2 to saves and +1 to attack and damage rolls instead.
+1 Charisma. When you score a Critical Hit, you and allies within 5 feet have Resistance to all damage and enemies within 5 feet have Vulnerability to all damage until the end of your next turn.
+1 Wisdom or Charisma. Advantage on saves against Frightened, and end Frightened on yourself as a Bonus Action Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest.
+1 Charisma. If a Heroic Inspiration reroll fails, it isn't expended (but can't be reused on that test). Using Heroic Inspiration heals you by the die roll, with any excess as Temporary Hit Points.
+1 Strength. Advantage on Charisma (Deception, Intimidation, and Persuasion) checks with warriors and martial folk, and add your Strength modifier to Inspiring Leader's Temporary Hit Points.

Automatically succeed on Strength checks to move through rough water. Immune to frigid water for hours equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Long and High Jumps while swimming (10 feet of swimming is a running start). Advantage on Initiative when starting combat partly submerged.

+1 Charisma. As a Bonus Action, taunt a creature within 30 feet that can hear and understand you: on a failed Charisma save (DC 8 + Charisma modifier + Proficiency Bonus) it takes -1 to attacks against you. Repeat each turn with a Bonus Action to stack penalties up to your Charisma modifier (new save each time). Ends if you drop to 0, are Incapacitated, skip a Bonus Action, it moves over 30 feet away, or after Proficiency Bonus rounds. A success grants 24-hour immunity.
+1 Strength or Charisma. +2 damage against Frightened creatures, and Frightened durations you cause are doubled.
+1 Constitution. Once per day a Short Rest removes 1 Exhaustion level, and a Long Rest removes 2.

+1 to any ability. Proficiency with an Artisan's Tool, or Advantage with one you already know. In combat, as a Bonus Action craft one item from the Fast Crafting table with proficient tools; it lasts until the end of your next turn or until you craft another. You can also craft one during a Short Rest, lasting until the end of the day or your next Long Rest.

+1 Strength. Jump distances +10 feet, and Advantage on attacks, Acrobatics, and Athletics checks right after jumping at least 10 feet high or 20 feet long. When you fall into liquid, a Reaction and a DC 15 Athletics or Acrobatics check (with Advantage) negates the fall damage.

+1 Wisdom. Advantage on Perception checks in Bright Light and no Disadvantage on Perception in Dim Light. Proficiency in Survival, snow and ice count as normal terrain, and Advantage on Survival in snow or ice.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. You know Frostbite or Ray of Frost, and always have Gust of Wind and one level 1 Cold-damage Druid, Sorcerer, or Wizard spell prepared, each castable once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots.
+1 Strength or Dexterity. Within 5 feet of a Large or larger creature, Dodge as a Bonus Action. Large or larger creatures have Disadvantage on saves against your Topple mastery.
+1 Dexterity or Constitution. After each Long Rest, gain Resistance to one damage type of your choice until your next Long Rest.
+1 Strength or Constitution. Resistance to Cold damage, and when you would take Fire damage, use your Reaction to gain Resistance to Fire until the start of your next turn.

name: Greater Blessing of Freyr and Freyja
spoken: greater blessing of freyr and freyja

display.prerequisite: Level 4+, Blessing of Freyr and Freyja Feat
display.description: +1 Wisdom or Charisma. Cure Wounds always prepared, castable without a slot Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest or with slots; healing is doubled on Beasts and Plants.

+1 Strength or Charisma. As an action, up to Proficiency Bonus creatures within 30 feet that can see you make a Wisdom save (DC 8 + Charisma modifier + Proficiency Bonus) or are Frightened for 1 minute (save each turn). Proficiency Bonus uses per Long Rest.
+1 Intelligence or Charisma. Advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks. Alter Self always prepared, once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots.
+1 Dexterity or Constitution. As a Bonus Action, for 1 minute your ranged weapon hits deal extra damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus once per turn. Proficiency Bonus uses per Long Rest.
+1 Strength or Constitution. As a Bonus Action, for 1 minute your melee weapon hits deal extra damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus once per turn. Proficiency Bonus uses per Long Rest.
+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. Advantage on checks with your Lore Bound skill. Augury always prepared, once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots.

+1 Constitution or Charisma. On a Critical Hit, +10 feet Speed and Advantage on attacks until the end of your next turn. When you drop a creature to 0 with an attack, an ally within 30 feet gains Heroic Inspiration to use by the end of its next turn (twice per Short or Long Rest).

+1 Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution. Advantage on Initiative at the start of a duel. As a Bonus Action, a successful Charisma (Intimidation) check against your duel opponent gives you Advantage on your next attack against it and it Disadvantage on its next attack against you.
+1 Wisdom or Intelligence. Advantage on Perception and Survival checks to follow or identify tracks, and on Stealth checks outdoors.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest, when a spell of level 1+ deals Cold damage to a creature, add one: Disadvantage on Dexterity checks for 1 minute; Restrained in ice until it saves (Dexterity) or takes 10 Bludgeoning or Fire; or Vulnerability to Cold for 1 minute (Constitution save each turn).

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest, when a spell of level 1+ deals Lightning damage to a creature, add one: Stunned until the end of your next turn if it failed its save; half the Lightning damage again at the start of its next turn (save negates); or Vulnerability to Lightning for 1 minute (Constitution save each turn).

+1 Constitution or Wisdom. A Long Rest in a natural area yields materials for a Healer's Kit and food for one Medium creature for a day. In 30 minutes build a shelter for 4 to 5 Medium humanoids; inside, they automatically succeed on saves against extreme cold and heat.
+1 Strength. Reach weapon attacks ignore a target's Shield bonus to AC, and you have +1 AC while wielding a Reach weapon.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. You know Dancing Lights or Light, and always have Moonbeam and one level 1 light spell from the Druid, Sorcerer, or Wizard list prepared, each castable once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots.

display.prerequisite: Level 4+, Strength or Dexterity 13+, Proficiency in Animal Handling
display.description: +1 Strength or Dexterity. Your mount's jump distance is doubled. Jumping from a moving mount uses its Speed if better; a melee hit after the jump adds 1d8 damage or knocks a target up to one size larger Prone (once per turn).

+1 Constitution. Advantage on saves against extreme cold (and against Cold damage if you already resist it). Your first Exhaustion level each day doesn't reduce your Speed, and you can ignore Exhaustion on a d20 Test.
+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. Barkskin and two of Animal Friendship, Entangle, Goodberry, or Speak with Animals always prepared, each castable once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots.
+1 Intelligence or Wisdom. Proficiency in Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, or Religion. Give yourself Advantage when you take the Study action, Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest.

display.prerequisite: Level 4+, Strength or Dexterity 13+, Weapon Mastery class feature
display.description: +1 Strength or Dexterity. +1 AC while holding a Spear, thrown Spear range 30/90, and Advantage on Readied Spear attacks.
+1 Strength or Constitution. As a Bonus Action, for 1 minute your melee weapon hits deal extra Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Proficiency Bonus uses per Long Rest.
+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. Hideous Laughter and two level 1 Enchantment or Illusion spells always prepared, each castable once per Long Rest without a slot or with slots.
+1 Intelligence. Advantage on Intelligence (Nature) checks, and you can find food and water for yourself and up to three others each day.

When you hit a creature within 5 feet that is no more than one size larger with an Unarmed Strike, you can force a Strength save (DC 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Strength modifier) or it has the Prone condition.
If you move at least 15 feet and stop within 5 feet of an ally, you have Advantage on attacks against creatures within 5 feet of that ally.
On your first melee weapon attack each turn, you can attack savagely: add your Proficiency Bonus to melee weapon damage rolls but take -2 AC until the start of your next turn.
When a creature you can see hits an adjacent ally, use your Reaction to add your Shield's AC bonus to the ally against that attack. You and an adjacent ally both wielding shields each gain +1 AC.
+10 feet Speed. Once per turn, after moving at least 15 feet, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage of a Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing hit.
You can end your move in the space of a creature two sizes larger. While sharing its space you have Advantage on attacks against it and it has Disadvantage on attacks against you.
After moving 15 feet or more toward a creature, +2 to your next Melee weapon or Unarmed Strike attack roll against it, or +2 to the save DC of a Grapple or Shove against it.

display.prerequisite: Lived in Yatamon for at least 1 year
display.description: Proficiency in the Salvage skill (Expertise if already proficient). You learn Naku Naku and Torum. Twice per Long Rest, when targeted by a level 1+ spell from yourself or an ally, regain Hit Points equal to twice the spell's level. You learn one Wizard cantrip.

+1 Constitution or Wisdom. A satisfying meal during a rest grants Heroic Inspiration or 1d10 + level Temporary Hit Points. Advantage on Charisma checks at formal events. Proficiency with Brewer's Supplies or Cook's Utensils, and 10 minutes identifies an ingredient's or potion's properties.

Advantage against the Prone condition, and standing costs at most 10 feet. Speak with felines as if by Speak with Animals. Add half your Proficiency Bonus to Wisdom (Perception) checks, even if already proficient.

+1 Intelligence or Charisma. When a creature within 10 feet fails a Charisma D20 Test, gain Advantage on your next Intimidation or Persuasion against it within an hour, or Heroic Inspiration (once per Long Rest). Reroll a failed Charisma check or save, but the DC rises by 3. 5 percent off purchases, and spend Heroic Inspiration for a further 10 + 1d10 percent.
+1 Dexterity or Intelligence. Vehicles you drive get +1 AC, you add your Proficiency Bonus to Maneuvering checks, small vehicles count as Nimble and Simple for you, and you add it to ram save DCs.

display.prerequisite: Level 4+, Member of the Yoka Scouts
display.description: +1 Strength or Dexterity. When an ally misses a creature within 10 feet of you, take a Reaction to let it reroll; if it hits, regain the Reaction (half Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest). +2 to ability checks an ally succeeded on in the last minute. Advantage on Search checks related to Demons.
Once per Long Rest, turn a failed save against Charmed or Frightened into a success. Whenever you roll a 1 on a D20 Test, you gain Heroic Inspiration.

Add your Proficiency Bonus to saves against Frightened. You need half the food and water and have Advantage on Survival checks to forage. Once per Short or Long Rest, gain Heroic Inspiration right after damage makes you Bloodied.

+1 Strength or Dexterity. Wield a Two-Handed weapon in one hand if the other hand holds no Two-Handed weapon or Shield. After attacking with a Two-Handed weapon in the Attack action, make a Bonus Action attack with a Light weapon (no ability modifier to damage unless negative or you have Two-Weapon Fighting).

+1 Strength. Proficiency with Cannons; reload one as a Bonus Action if you haven't moved (Speed 0 afterward). From level 11 it doesn't stop you and can replace an attack; at level 20 ignore the Artillery property. Double damage to objects and structures, and Cannons and Cannonballs weigh half for you.
Once per Long Rest while Bloodied, treat a hit's damage roll as the maximum. If Frightened at the start of your turn, roll a d20; on 10 or higher the condition ends.

Attack without ending the Invisible condition, Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest. You can hide from larger creatures while lightly obscured or more than 30 feet away. Perception checks to detect you while Invisible have Disadvantage.

If Charmed at the start of your turn, roll a d20; on 10 or higher it ends. Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest, tell whether an NPC speaking to you is knowingly lying. Advantage on Insight checks against creatures you are speaking with.
Learn three languages. Proficiency Bonus times per Long Rest, give a spell's save DC +2, but you are Paralyzed until the start of your next turn.

name: I Survived to Tell the Tale
spoken: i survived to tell the tale

display.description: Once per Long Rest when damage would drop you to 0, regain Hit Points equal to your level. +10 feet Speed. When you would be Grappled, roll a d20; on 10 or higher you aren't.
Proficiency in one skill of your choice, and Expertise in that skill.
You can breathe underwater (removing any Limited Amphibiousness dependence on water), gain proficiency in Athletics, and have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.
Proficiency with one tool of your choice. One tool you're proficient with is built into your body and can't be removed; with a hand free you can use it, and add 1d4 to ability checks made with it.
Proficiency and Expertise in Stealth. When you take the Hide action, the DC to succeed is 10.

Define two personas. Adept Persona: while in it, proficiency with a chosen tool and +1d4 to checks with it. Expert Persona: while in it, Expertise in a chosen skill you're proficient in. You also know Skin Cant.

Your Mind Link reaches 120 feet or 10 times your level. You can message everyone you're linked to at once and let them talk telepathically with each other, and you can Help an ally's attack from any distance while linked.

display.prerequisite: Dhakaani Ghaal'dar, Dhakaani Golin'dar, or Dhakaani Guul'dar
display.description: You dream lucidly and remember your dreams. A spirit mentor in the Uul Dhakaan may send visions, missions, or clues after a Long Rest. Resistance to Psychic damage.
+1 Intelligence or Wisdom. Advantage on Death Saving Throws, Resistance to Necrotic and Radiant damage, and spells that deal Necrotic can deal Radiant instead.

+1 Constitution or Dexterity. +1 AC. Each time you use Shape-Shifter, gain one until you shift again: gills and a Swim Speed equal to your Speed; Darkvision 60 feet; or natural weapons (claws, fangs, horns, or hooves) dealing 1d6 with your Unarmed Strike, using Strength or Dexterity.
+1 Strength or Constitution. Armor you wear can't be targeted by effects against your will while you live, and Critical Hits against you become normal hits.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. Pick a quori lineage: Du'ulora (Intimidation, Crown of Madness), Hashalaq (Persuasion, Suggestion), Kalaraq (Perception, Mind Spike), or Tsucora (Intimidation, Shatter dealing Psychic). Add 1d4 to checks with that skill; the spell is always prepared, free once per Long Rest, and castable with slots.
+1 Strength, Dexterity, or Wisdom. You can shift at the start of your turn with no action, shifting lasts 10 minutes, and you gain one extra use (one use back on a Short Rest, all on a Long Rest).

Advantage on Investigation checks. True Seeing is always prepared, free once per Long Rest, and castable with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

Advantage on Perception checks. Commune with Nature and Find the Path are always prepared, each free once per Short Rest, and castable with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

Advantage on Animal Handling checks. Dominate Beast is always prepared, free once per Long Rest, and castable with slots; you have Advantage on its Concentration checks, it lasts up to 8 hours, and you can hold it while asleep. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

Advantage on Medicine checks. Heal is always prepared, free once per Long Rest, and castable with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

Advantage on Persuasion checks. Mordenkainen's Magnificent Mansion is always prepared, free once per Long Rest, and castable with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

Advantage on Investigation checks. Fabricate (free once per Short Rest) and Create Homunculus (free once per Long Rest) are always prepared and castable with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

Advantage on Acrobatics checks. Teleport is always prepared, free once per Long Rest, and castable with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

Advantage on Insight checks and Calligrapher's Supplies checks. Symbol is always prepared, free once per Long Rest, and castable with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

Advantage on Perception checks. Globe of Invulnerability is always prepared, free once per Long Rest, and castable with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

Advantage on Stealth checks. Project Image is always prepared, free once per Long Rest, and castable with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

Advantage on Acrobatics checks and Navigator's Tools checks. Control Weather is always prepared, free once per Long Rest, and castable with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

Advantage on Investigation checks and Thieves' Tools checks. Forbiddance is always prepared, free once per Long Rest, and castable with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (chosen on receipt). One Siberys mark per character.

+1 Wisdom or Charisma. Proficiency in Intimidation. When a creature you can see casts a spell, you have Advantage on attacks against it until the end of your next turn. With slots of each level, always prepared: Guiding Bolt, Shining Smite, Nondetection, Aura of Purity, Circle of Power.

+1 Wisdom or Charisma. Proficiency in Arcana. Add 1d4 to saves against an Aberration's spells or magical abilities. With slots of each level, always prepared: Detect Evil and Good, Warding Bond, Magic Circle, Banishment, Dispel Evil and Good.

+1 Wisdom or Charisma. Proficiency in Performance. When you Charm a creature, use your Reaction to move half your Speed without provoking. Your spells and abilities that affect Humanoids also affect Fey. With slots of each level, always prepared: Tasha's Hideous Laughter, Enthrall, Major Image, Compulsion, Mislead.

+1 Strength or Constitution. After a rest, set unarmored AC to 14 + Dexterity or 18 (shields still apply); your hide can be enchanted like armor; claws deal 1d6 + Strength Slashing with Unarmed Strikes.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. After a rest roll 1d6; once before it's lost, add it to a spell attack through an Orb or subtract it from one target's save. Holding an Orb, Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage, and when a creature enters within 5 feet you can use your Reaction to move your Speed without provoking.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. Through a Rod: reroll 1s and 2s on cantrip damage against targets within 20 feet, no Disadvantage on ranged spell attacks within 5 feet of an enemy, and after a ranged spell attack, a Bonus Action melee attack with the Rod as a Club.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. The Medusa Spells (Ensnaring Strike, Hold Person, Hypnotic Pattern, Stoneskin, Hold Monster) are always prepared as you reach their levels, each free once per Long Rest and castable with slots, using your Petrifying Gaze ability.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. Through a Staff: Bonus Action to double a spell's range, reroll 1s and 2s on cantrip damage, and if every target is beyond half range, one creature you hit or that fails its save is knocked Prone.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. When a creature you Restrained or Paralyzed fails its save to end it by 5 or more, you can Petrify it for 1 minute with Concentration; held the full minute, it stays stone until Greater Restoration.

+1 Dexterity, Wisdom, or Charisma. The Harpy Spells (Charm Person, Suggestion, Enemies Abound, Charm Monster, Dominate Person) are always prepared as you reach their levels, each free once per Long Rest and castable with slots, using your Harpy's Charms ability.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. Through a Wand: Advantage on spell attacks against targets that haven't taken a turn, no Disadvantage on ranged spell attacks within 5 feet of an enemy, and drawing or stowing a Wand is free.

+1 Wisdom or Charisma. Proficiency in Animal Handling. Once per Short or Long Rest, when a creature hits another within 5 feet of you, use your Reaction to reduce the damage by 1d6 + Proficiency Bonus. With slots of each level, always prepared: Sanctuary, Detect Thoughts, Blink, Mordenkainen's Faithful Hound, Hold Monster.
+1 Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution. You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

+1 Wisdom or Constitution. Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus after taking Necrotic damage, and creatures you conjure can be Undead. With slots of each level, always prepared: False Life, Ray of Enfeeblement, Bestow Curse, Death Ward, Enervation.
+1 to attack rolls with spells, and +1 to the save DC of your cantrips.
Survival rolls of 1 to 9 count as 10 when identifying remains; Expertise in Survival when tracking beasts; the first time you meet a new beast, learn its AC, maximum HP, or one Resistance.
A belt lamp (20 feet bright, 20 dim); Tremorsense 30 feet underground (+20 if you already have it); Advantage on checks and saves to escape falling natural rock.
+1 Wisdom. Cast Stone Shape without materials or a slot once per day (3 at level 10, 5 at 15, unlimited at 20). Tremorsense 10 feet.
+1 Intelligence. Expertise in Animal Handling, and creatures you tame gain +1 to AC, attack rolls, and damage.
+1 Strength or Constitution. Advantage on Animal Handling, Beasts have Disadvantage on saves against your Grapple, and a Small to Large Beast you grapple can't target you.
+1 Intelligence or Constitution. Resistance to Fire. Study a visible volcano for 10 minutes to estimate when it will erupt, and the safe distance if within 7 days.
+1 Strength or Dexterity. When a bite or maw attack hits you, use your Reaction to reduce the damage by 1d10 + your level. Your first failed Athletics check each day succeeds instead.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. As an Action, enchant one touched item for 1 minute: a weapon deals +1d6 of a damage type your spells deal (+PB at 16); armor grants Resistance to one such type (two at 16); a wondrous item grants Advantage against one condition (two at 16). One enchantment at a time.

You have honed your martial prowess and gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see "Feats"). Defense is recommended.

Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

Because your magic flows from within, you can alter your spells to suit your needs; you gain two Metamagic options of your choice from "Metamagic Options" later in this class's description. You use the chosen options to temporarily modify spells you cast. To use an option, you must spend the number of Sorcery Points that it costs.

You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it unless otherwise noted in one of those options.

Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your Metamagic options with one you don't know. You gain two more options at Sorcerer level 10 and two more at Sorcerer level 17.

You have unearthed Eldritch Invocations, pieces of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability or other lessons. You gain one invocation of your choice, such as Pact of the Tome. Invocations are described in the "Eldritch Invocation Options" section later in this class's description.

Prerequisites. If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. For example, if an invocation requires you to be a level 5+ Warlock, you can select the invocation once you reach Warlock level 5.

Replacing and Gaining Invocations. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify. You can't replace an invocation if it's a prerequisite for another invocation that you have.

When you gain certain Warlock levels, you gain more invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations column of the Warlock Features table.

You can't pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.

Cost: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can protect some of those creatures from the spell's full force. To do so, spend 1 Sorcery Point and choose a number of those creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the spell, and
it takes no damage if it would normally take half damage on a successful save.

Cost: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell that has a range of at least 5 feet, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to double the spell's range. Or when you cast a spell that has a range of Touch, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to make the spell's range 30 feet.

Cost: 1 Sorcery Point

When you roll damage for a spell, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one), and you must use the new rolls.

You can use Empowered Spell even if you've already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

Cost: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to double its duration to a maximum duration of 24 hours.

If the affected spell requires Concentration, you have Advantage on any saving throw you make to maintain that Concentration.

Cost: 2 Sorcery Points

When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can spend 2 Sorcery Points to give one target of the spell Disadvantage on saves against the spell.

Cost: 2 Sorcery Points

When you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action, you can spend 2 Sorcery Points to change the casting time to a Bonus Action for this casting. You can't modify a spell in this way if you've already cast a level 1+ spell on the current turn, nor can you cast a level 1+ spell on this turn after modifying a spell in this way.

Cost: 1 Sorcery Point

If you make an attack roll for a spell and miss, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to reroll the d20, and you must use the new roll.

You can use Seeking Spell even if you've already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

Cost: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to cast it without any Verbal, Somatic, or Material components, except Material components that are consumed by the spell or that have a cost specified in the spell.

Cost: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell that deals a type of damage from the following list, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to change that damage type to one of the other listed types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, Thunder.

Cost: 1 Sorcery Point

When you cast a spell, such as Charm Person, that can be cast with a higher-level spell slot to target an additional creature, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to increase the spell's effective level by 1.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage

Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage. You can add your Charisma modifier to that spell's damage rolls.

Repeatable. You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different eligible cantrip.
You can cast Mage Armor on yourself without expending a spell slot.

Prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock

You can cast Levitate on yourself without expending a spell slot.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock

You can see normally in Dim Light and Darkness - both magical and nonmagical - within 120 feet of yourself.

Prerequisite: Level 12+ Warlock, Thirsting Blade Invocation

The Extra Attack of your Thirsting Blade invocation confers two extra attacks rather than one.
You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain Concentration.

Prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock, Pact of the Blade Invocation

Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to deal an extra 1d8 Force damage to the target,
plus another 1d8 per level of the spell slot, and you can give the target the Prone condition if it is Huge or smaller.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage

Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage and has a range of 10+ feet. When you cast that spell, its range increases by a number of feet equal to 30 times your Warlock level.

Repeatable. You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different eligible cantrip.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock

You can cast False Life on yourself without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell with this feature, you don't roll the die for the Temporary Hit Points; you automatically get the highest number on the die.

Prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock

You can use a Bonus Action to touch a willing creature and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn. As long as the creature is on the same plane of existence as you, you can take a Bonus Action on subsequent turns to maintain this connection, extending the duration until the end of your next turn. The connection ends if you don't maintain it in this way.

While perceiving through the other creature's senses, you benefit from any special senses possessed by that creature, and you can cast spells as if you were in your space or the other creature's space if the two of you are within 60 feet of each other.

Prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock

You can breathe underwater, and you gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

You can also cast Water Breathing once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way again when you finish a Long Rest.

Prerequisite: Level 9+ Warlock, Pact of the Tome Invocation

A new page appears in your Book of Shadows when you conjure it. With your permission, a creature can take an action to write its name on that page, which can contain a number of names equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one name).

When any creature whose name is on the page is reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, the creature magically drops to 1 Hit Point instead. Once this magic is triggered, no creature can benefit from it until you finish a Long Rest.

As a Magic action, you can erase a name on the page by touching it.

Prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock, Pact of the Chain Invocation

When you cast Find Familiar, you infuse the summoned familiar with a measure of your eldritch power, granting the creature the following benefits.

Aerial or Aquatic. The familiar gains either a Fly Speed or a Swim Speed (your choice) of 40 feet.

Quick Attack. As a Bonus Action, you can command the familiar to take the Attack action.

Necrotic or Radiant Damage. Whenever the familiar deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can make it deal Necrotic or Radiant damage instead.

Your Save DC. If the familiar forces a creature to make a saving throw, it uses your spell save DC.

Resistance. When the familiar takes damage, you can take a Reaction to grant it Resistance against that damage.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock

You have received knowledge from an elder entity of the multiverse, allowing you to gain one Origin feat of your choice (see "Feats").

Repeatable. You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different Origin feat.

Prerequisite: Level 9+ Warlock, Pact of the Blade Invocation

Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage (your choice) to the creature, and you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice to roll it and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 Hit Point).

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock

You can cast Disguise Self without expending a spell slot.

Prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock

You can cast Alter Self without expending a spell slot.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock

You can cast Silent Image without expending a spell slot.

Prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock

While you're in an area of Dim Light or Darkness, you can cast Invisibility on yourself without expending a spell slot.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock

You can cast Jump on yourself without expending a spell slot.

As a Bonus Action, you can conjure a pact weapon in your hand - a Simple or Martial Melee weapon of your choice with which you bond - or create a bond with a magic weapon you touch; you can't bond with a magic weapon if someone else is attuned to it or another Warlock is bonded with it. Until the bond ends, you have proficiency with the weapon, and you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus.

Whenever you attack with the bonded weapon, you can use your Charisma modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity; and you can cause the weapon to deal Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage or its normal damage type.

Your bond with the weapon ends if you use this feature's Bonus Action again, if the weapon is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more, or if you die. A conjured weapon disappears when the bond ends.

You learn the Find Familiar spell and can cast it as a Magic action without expending a spell slot.

When you cast the spell, you choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: Imp, Pseudodragon, Quasit, Skeleton, Sphinx of Wonder, Sprite, or Venomous Snake (see "Monsters" for the familiar's stat block).

Additionally, when you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its Reaction.

Stitching together strands of shadow, you conjure forth a book in your hand at the end of a Short or Long Rest. This Book of Shadows (you determine its appearance) contains eldritch magic that only you can access, granting you the benefits below. The book disappears if you conjure another book with this feature or if you die.

Cantrips and Rituals. When the book appears, choose three cantrips, and choose two level 1 spells that have the Ritual tag. The spells can be from any class's spell list, and they must be spells you don't already have prepared. While the book is on your person, you have the chosen spells prepared, and they function as Warlock spells for you.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use the book as a Spellcasting Focus.

Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage via an Attack Roll

Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that requires an attack roll. When you hit a Large or smaller creature with that cantrip, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from you.

Repeatable. You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different eligible cantrip.

Prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock, Pact of the Blade Invocation

You gain the Extra Attack feature for your pact weapon only. With that feature, you can attack twice with the weapon instead of once when you take the Attack action on your turn.

Prerequisite: Level 9+ Warlock

You can cast Arcane Eye without expending a spell slot.

Prerequisite: Level 7+ Warlock

You can cast Speak with Dead without expending a spell slot.

Prerequisite: Level 15+ Warlock

You have Truesight with a range of 30 feet.

You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a Bonus Action if you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

You can enter your Rage the number of times shown for your Barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian Features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

While active, your Rage follows the rules below. Damage Resistance. You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Rage Damage. When you make an attack using Strength - with either a weapon or an Unarmed Strike - and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain levels as a Barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian Features table.

Strength Advantage. You have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

No Concentration or Spells. You can't maintain Concentration, and you can't cast spells.

Duration. The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the Incapacitated condition. If your Rage is still active on your next turn, you can extend the Rage for another round by doing one of the following:
- Make an attack roll against an enemy.
- Force an enemy to make a saving throw.
- Take a Bonus Action to extend your Rage.

Each time the Rage is extended, it lasts until the end of your next turn. You can maintain a Rage for up to 10 minutes.
While you aren't wearing any armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Constitution modifiers. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice, such as Greataxes and Handaxes. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Barbarian levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Barbarian Features table.
You gain an uncanny sense of when things aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge perils. You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with increased ferocity. When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you Advantage on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have Advantage during that time.

You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1.

In addition, while your Rage is active, you can channel primal power when you attempt certain tasks; whenever you make an ability check using one of the following skills, you can make it as a Strength check even if it normally uses a different ability: Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, or Survival. When you use this ability, your Strength represents primal power coursing through you, honing your agility, bearing, and senses.
You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor.
Your instincts are so honed that you have Advantage on Initiative rolls.
As part of the Bonus Action you take to enter your Rage, you can move up to half your Speed.

If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any Advantage on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn't have Disadvantage. If the chosen attack roll hits, the target takes an extra 1d10 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon or Unarmed Strike, and you can cause one Brutal Strike effect of your choice. You have the following effect options.

Forceful Blow. The target is pushed 15 feet straight away from you. You can then move up to half your Speed straight toward the target without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Hamstring Blow. The target's Speed is reduced by 15 feet until the start of your next turn. A target can be affected by only one Hamstring Blow at a time the most recent one.

Your Rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 Hit Points while your Rage is active and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, your Hit Points instead change to a number equal to twice your Barbarian level.

Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, the DC resets to 10.

You have honed new ways to attack furiously. The following effects are now among your Brutal Strike options.

Staggering Blow. The target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes, and it can't make Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn.

Sundering Blow. Before the start of your next turn, the next attack roll made by another creature against the target gains a +5 bonus to the roll. An attack roll can gain only one Sundering Blow bonus.

When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended uses of Rage. After you regain uses of Rage in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

In addition, your Rage is so fierce that it now lasts for 10 minutes without you needing to do anything to extend it from round to round. Your Rage ends early if you have the Unconscious condition (not just the Incapacitated condition) or don Heavy armor.
The extra damage of your Brutal Strike increases to 2d10. In addition, you can use two different Brutal Strike effects whenever you use your Brutal Strike feature.
If your total for a Strength check or Strength saving throw is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.
You embody primal power. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. This inspiration is represented by your Bardic Inspiration die, which is a d6.

Using Bardic Inspiration. As a Bonus Action, you can inspire another creature within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. That creature gains one of your Bardic Inspiration dice. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.

Once within the next hour when the creature fails a D20 Test, the creature can roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning the failure into a success. A Bardic Inspiration die is expended when it's rolled.

Number of Uses. You can confer a Bardic Inspiration die a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

At Higher Levels. Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain Bard levels, as shown in the Bardic Die column of the Bard Features table. The die becomes a d8 at level 5, a d10 at level 10, and a d12 at level 15.

You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Bard spells, which appear in the Bard spell list later in the class's description.

Cantrips. You know two cantrips of your choice from the Bard spell list. Dancing Lights and Vicious Mockery are recommended.

Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Bard spell list.

When you reach Bard levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Bard spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Bard Features table.

Spell Slots. The Bard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Bard spell list. Charm Person, Color Spray, Dissonant Whispers, and Healing Word are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Bard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Bard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Bard spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Bard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

If another Bard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Bard spells for you.

Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Bard spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Bard spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Musical Instrument as a Spellcasting Focus for your Bard spells.

You gain Expertise (see "Rules Glossary") in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. Performance and Persuasion are recommended if you have proficiency in them.

At Bard level 9, you gain Expertise in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to any ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack and that doesn't otherwise use your Proficiency Bonus.

For example, if you make a Strength (Athletics) check and lack Athletics proficiency, you can add half your Proficiency Bonus to the check.

You now regain all your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

In addition, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one expended use of Bardic Inspiration.

You can use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. If you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against an effect that applies the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can take a Reaction to cause the save to be rerolled, and the new roll has Advantage.

You've learned secrets from various magical traditions. Whenever you reach a Bard level (including this level) and the Prepared Spells number in the Bard Features table increases, you can choose any of your new prepared spells from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, and Wizard spell lists, and the chosen spells count as Bard spells for you (see a class's section for its spell list). In addition, whenever you replace a spell prepared for this class, you can replace it with a spell from those lists.
When you roll Initiative, you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that.

You have mastered two of the Words of Creation: the words of life and death. You therefore always have the Power Word Heal and Power Word Kill spells prepared. When you cast either spell, you can target a second creature with it if that creature is within 10 feet of the first target.

You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.

Protector. Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Heavy armor.

Thaumaturge. You know one extra cantrip from the Cleric spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to the divine gives you a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) checks. The bonus equals your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).

You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Divine Spark and Turn Undead, each of which is described below. Each time you use this class's Channel Divinity, choose which Channel Divinity effect from this class to create. You gain additional effect options at higher Cleric levels.

You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You gain additional uses when you reach certain Cleric levels, as shown in the Channel Divinity column of the Cleric Features table.

If a Channel Divinity effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals the spell save DC from this class's Spellcasting feature.

Divine Spark. As a Magic action, you point your Holy Symbol at another creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself and focus divine energy at it. Roll 1d8 and add your Wisdom modifier. You either restore Hit Points to the creature equal to that total or force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice) equal to that total. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage (round down).

You roll an additional d8 when you reach Cleric levels 7 (2d8), 13 (3d8), and 18 (4d8).

Turn Undead. As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and censure Undead creatures. Each Undead of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its save, it has the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions for 1 minute. For that duration, it tries to move as far from you as it can on its turns. This effect ends early on the creature if it takes any damage, if you have the Incapacitated condition, or if you die.

Whenever you use Turn Undead, you can roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1d8) and add the rolls together. Each Undead that fails its saving throw against that use of Turn Undead takes Radiant damage equal to the roll's total. This damage doesn't end the turn effect.

Divine power infuses you in battle. You gain one of the following options of your choice (if you get either option from a Cleric subclass in an older book, use only the option you choose for this feature).

Divine Strike. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can cause the target to take an extra 1d8 Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice).

Potent Spellcasting. Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Cleric cantrip.

You can call on your deity or pantheon to intervene on your behalf. As a Magic action, choose any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that doesn't require a Reaction to cast. As part of the same action, you cast that spell without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. You can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

The option you chose for Blessed Strikes grows more powerful.

Divine Strike. The extra damage of your Divine Strike increases to 2d8.

Potent Spellcasting. When you cast a Cleric cantrip and deal damage to a creature with it, you can give vitality to yourself or another creature within 60 feet of yourself, granting a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Wisdom modifier.

You can call on even more powerful divine intervention. When you use your Divine Intervention feature, you can choose Wish when you select a spell. If you do so, you can't use Divine Intervention again until you finish 2d4 Long Rests.

You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids. While learning this ancient tongue, you also unlocked the magic of communicating with animals; you always have the Speak with Animals spell prepared.

You can use Druidic to leave hidden messages. You and others who know Druidic automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check but can't decipher it without magic.

You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.

Magician. You know one extra cantrip from the Druid spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to nature gives you a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Nature) checks. The bonus equals your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

Warden. Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor.

You can summon a nature spirit that assumes an animal form to aid you. As a Magic action, you can expend a spell slot or a use of Wild Shape to cast the Find Familiar spell without Material components.

When you cast the spell in this way, the familiar is Fey and disappears when you finish a Long Rest.

The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a Bonus Action, you shape-shift into a Beast form that you have learned for this feature (see "Known Forms" below). You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level or until you use Wild Shape again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die. You can also leave the form early as a Bonus Action.

Number of Uses. You can use Wild Shape twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

You gain additional uses when you reach certain Druid levels, as shown in the Wild Shape column of the Druid Features table.

Known Forms. You know four Beast forms for this feature, chosen from among Beast stat blocks that have a maximum Challenge Rating of 1/4 and that lack a Fly Speed (see "Animals" in "Monsters" for stat block options). The Rat, Riding Horse, Spider, and Wolf are recommended. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your known forms with another eligible form.

When you reach certain Druid levels, your number of known forms and the maximum Challenge Rating for those forms increases, as shown in the Beast Shapes table. In addition, starting at level 8, you can adopt a form that has a Fly Speed.

When choosing known forms, you may look in other sources for eligible Beasts if the Game Master permits you to do so.

Table: Beast Shapes

|Druid Level|Known Forms|Max CR|Fly Speed|
|---|---|---|---|
|2|4|1/4|No|
|4|6|1/2|No|
|8|8|1|Yes|

Rules While Shape-Shifted. While in a form, you retain your personality, memories, and ability to speak, and the following rules apply:
- Temporary Hit Points. When you assume a Wild Shape form, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to your Druid level.
- Game Statistics. Your game statistics are replaced by the Beast's stat block, but you retain your creature type; Hit Points; Hit Point Dice; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. You also retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies and use your Proficiency Bonus for them, in addition to gaining the proficiencies of the creature. If a skill or saving throw modifier in the Beast's stat block is higher than yours, use the one in the stat block.
- No Spellcasting. You can't cast spells, but shapeshifting doesn't break your Concentration or otherwise interfere with a spell you've already cast.
- Objects. Your ability to handle objects is determined by the form's limbs rather than your own. In addition, you choose whether your equipment falls in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the GM decides whether it's practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment based on the creature's size and shape. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with the form. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect while you're in that form.

Once on each of your turns, if you have no uses of Wild Shape left, you can give yourself one use by expending a spell slot (no action required).

In addition, you can expend one use of Wild Shape (no action required) to give yourself a level 1 spell slot, but you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

The might of the elements flows through you. You gain one of the following options of your choice.

Potent Spellcasting. Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Druid cantrip.

Primal Strike. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon or a Beast form's attack in Wild Shape, you can cause the target to take an extra 1d8 Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage (choose when you hit).

The option you chose for Elemental Fury grows more powerful, as detailed below.

Potent Spellcasting. When you cast a Druid cantrip with a range of 10 feet or greater, the spell's range increases by 300 feet.

Primal Strike. The extra damage of your Primal Strike increases to 2d8.
While using Wild Shape, you can cast spells in Beast form, except for any spell that has a Material component with a cost specified or that consumes its Material component.

The vitality of nature constantly blooms within you, granting you the following benefits.

Evergreen Wild Shape. Whenever you roll Initiative and have no uses of Wild Shape left, you regain one expended use of it.

Nature Magician. You can convert uses of Wild Shape into a spell slot (no action required). Choose a number of your unexpended uses of Wild Shape and convert them into a single spell slot, with each use contributing 2 spell levels. For example, if you convert two uses of Wild Shape, you produce a level 4 spell slot. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

Longevity. The primal magic that you wield causes you to age more slowly. For every ten years that pass, your body ages only one year.

You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a Bonus Action, you can use it to regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level.

You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter Features table.

You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the Magic action.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.

You have a mind for tactics on and off the battlefield. When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success. Rather than regaining Hit Points, you roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn't expended.
Whenever you activate your Second Wind with a Bonus Action, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.
When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the Push, Sap, or Slow property for that attack.
You can attack three times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

You study your opponents and learn from each attack you make. If you make an attack roll against a creature and miss, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.
You can attack four times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use your Unarmed Strike and Monk weapons, which are the following:

- Simple Melee weapons
- Martial Melee weapons that have the Light property
